summary: Lati Rinpoche (1922–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery, where he later served as abbot (~1976–1984), and was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia (~1976–1977).

Latika Lahiri (1923–2008) was a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University in 1958 under supervisor Xianlin Ji, and held an academic post at the University of Delhi from around 1969 to 1988.

Laura Harrington is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and teachers including Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi, Gary A. Tubb, and Lobsang Jamspal.

Lauran Hartley is a scholar of Tibetology. She has held posts as a visiting assistant professor at Indiana University, an adjunct lecturer at Columbia University, a teacher at Rutgers University (attested 2003), and a consultant and editor at Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003).

Laurence Austine Waddell (1854–1938) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying medicine at the University of Glasgow (~1874–1878), he served in the British Army (~1880–1917), at Kolkata's Medical College (1896), and as professor of Tibetan at University College London (1906–1908).

Laurie L. Patton (born 1961) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She studied at Harvard University and earned her doctorate at the University of Chicago (~1985–1991), later holding posts at Emory (~1996–2011), Duke (~2011–2015), and Middlebury College (~2015–2024).

Lawrence E. Sullivan is a religious studies scholar. He served as Director at Harvard University (attested 2000–2004) and as a professor in the Department of Theology at the University of Notre Dame (attested 2005).

Lawrence McCrea is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Cornell University and the University of Chicago, working under Sheldon Pollock (~1992–1998), and took up a post at Cornell University around 2009.

Lawrence William Nelson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed a Doctor of Philosophy and Religion at the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2012) and also studied at Butler, Indiana, New York, Northwestern, and St. John's College.

Le Manh That (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Saigon (~1962–1965) and earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1974), later holding a post at Van Hanh University (~1974–1975).

LeRoy Carr Barret (1877–1960) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed his education at Washington and Lee University (~1895–1898) and Johns Hopkins University (~1899–1903), where he studied under Maurice Bloomfield.

Leah Judith Zahler specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under the doctoral supervision of Jeffrey Hopkins (1980–1981), also studying under Harvey B. Aronson, Joe Bransford Wilson, and Geshe Wangyal.

Leedom Lefferts is a scholar in religious studies and anthropology. He has served as Professor Emeritus of Anthropology at Drew University (attested 2011) and as a research associate in the Department of Anthropology at the Smithsonian Institution (attested 2011).

Leela Aditi Wood specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Michigan (until 2005) under doctoral supervisors Luis Oscar Gómez and Martin J. Powers, and held a post at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Leo M. Pruden (1937–1991) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taitetsu Unno and Akira Hirakawa at the University of Tokyo (1964–1966). He held posts at Brown University (1970–1971), Nyingma Institute (1971), and the University of Oriental Studies (attested 1988).

Leo Meyer (1830–1910) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and in Berlin under Franz Bopp and Moriz Haupt, later holding posts at the University of Göttingen (~1862–1865) and the Imperial University of Dorpat (~1865–1898).

Leon Hurvitz (1923–1992) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He served as a professor at the University of Washington (attested 1965–1973) and at the University of British Columbia (~1971–1988, attested 1990).

Leonard Bloomfield (1887–1949) was a linguist who studied at Harvard, Wisconsin, Chicago, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held academic posts at Cincinnati (~1909–1910), Illinois (~1913–1921), Ohio State (~1921–1927), Chicago (~1927–1940), and Yale (~1940–1949).

Leonard C. D. C. Priestley is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder and teacher F. E. L. Priestley, and held an academic post at the University of Toronto (attested 1991).

Leonard van der Kuijp (born 1952) is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his doctoral degrees under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg (~1976–1983) and held posts at the University of Washington (attested 1989–1996) and Harvard University (1995).
